cards.back: Smallest deployable unit in K8s. One or more containers sharing network/storage. Ephemeral - replaced when deleted.
Manages replicated Pods. Provides updates, rollbacks, scaling. Declarative state management.
Network endpoint for Pods. Stable IP/DNS. Load balances across Pods. Types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer.

cards.front: What's the difference: NodePort vs Service Port vs TargetPort?
cards.back: NodePort: external port on node. Service Port: port service listens on. TargetPort: port on container. Flow: NodePort → ServicePort → TargetPort → ContainerPort.
Storage resource in cluster. Represents piece of storage. Can be pre-provisioned or dynamic.
User's request for storage. Binds to a PV. Pods use PVC to mount storage.
Stores configuration data (key-value). Can be injected as env vars or mounted as files. Secrets for sensitive data.
Virtual cluster within K8s. Resource isolation. Same names can exist in different namespaces.
Controls traffic between Pods/Namesspaces. Whitelist model (deny all, allow specific). Ingress + egress rules.
HTTP/HTTPS route to Services. Host/path-based routing. Single IP for multiple services.
Hard requirement. Pod only schedules on nodes with matching labels. Simple scheduling.
More expressive scheduling. requiredDuringScheduling (hard) vs preferredDuringScheduling (soft with weights).
Node property that repels Pods. Effect: NoSchedule, NoExecute, PreferNoSchedule. Only Pods with toleration can schedule.
Pod property allowing it to schedule on tainted nodes. 'I can handle this taint.'
Role-Based Access Control. ServiceAccount → Role(permissions) → RoleBinding. ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding for cluster-wide.
Manages stateful apps. Stable network identity, stable storage, ordered deployment/scaling.
Cordon: mark node unschedulable (no new pods). Drain: cordon + evict existing pods (for maintenance).
Ensures Pod runs on every node. Used for logging, monitoring. drain --ignore-daemonsets needed because DaemonSet pods can't be evicted.
K8s key-value store. All cluster state stored here. Backup required for disaster recovery.
K8s API frontend. All requests go through it. Authenticates, validates, stores in etcd.
Decides which node runs a Pod. Considers resources, constraints, affinity, taints.
Runs controller processes. Node controller, Deployment controller, Endpoint controller, etc.
Agent on each node. Talks to apiserver. Ensures containers running as specified.
Network proxy on each node. Maintains network rules. Implements Service abstraction.
Tool to create K8s clusters. init (control-plane), join (workers), token create.
2 hours, 15-20 tasks, 67% pass. All hands-on, no multiple choice. Graded by cluster state, not commands. Docs available.

cards.front: Create a deployment 'web' with nginx:1.27, 3 replicas
Expose web deployment as NodePort service on port 30080
cards.back:
kubectl expose deployment web --port=80 --target-port=80 --type=NodePort --name=web-svc
Then edit to set nodePort: 30080

cards.front: Create a multi-container pod: nginx + busybox (sleep 3600)
cards.back:
kubectl run multitool --image=nginx --restart=Never --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
Then edit YAML to add second container.

cards.front: Node maintenance: cordon node1, drain it, uncordon after
cards.back:
kubectl cordon node1
kubectl drain node1 --ignore-daemonsets
# work done
kubectl uncordon node1

cards.front: Taint node 'worker1' with key=dedicated, value=worker, effect=NoSchedule
Add toleration to pod for taint 'dedicated=worker:NoSchedule'
cards.back:
Edit pod YAML to add:
tolerations:
- key: dedicated
  operator: Equal
  value: worker
  effect: NoSchedule
